Reusable helpers. Each takes its inputs as arguments and reads no global objects, and each is tested on synthetic data with a known answer in [`tests/test-functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/tests/test-functions.R).

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/functions.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Dialysis-facility-density-USRDS/blob/main/R/setup.R)

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/functions.R")
```

## Yes/no fields

The CMS-2728 form records comorbidities and insurance as yes, no or unknown. A condition counts as present only when a field is "YES"; missing or unknown counts as not present. The original code returned missing for missing fields, which would drop patients from the models; the published sample sizes show the paper's models did not.

**Used in:** 3. USRDS patient data ([Patient variables](prepare_patients.qmd#patient-variables)); [Insurance](#insurance) on this page.

```{r}
#| label: fn-any-yes
#| eval: false
```

## Insurance

The original code's hierarchy, unchanged: no insurance, then Medicaid, then Medicare (including Medicare Advantage), then employer group, then other (including VA).

## Nephrology care

Whether the patient saw a nephrologist before kidney failure: none, some or unknown, as in the paper's Table 1 and Model 3. Unknown is its own level, so the models keep the patients the paper kept.

**Used in:** 3. USRDS patient data ([Patient variables](prepare_patients.qmd#patient-variables)).

**Used in:** 1. Public area data ([HSA benchmarks](download_public_data.qmd#hsa-benchmarks)).

## Category labels

The labels of the five categories, built from the three cut points rounded to two decimals: 0, then >0 to the first cut point, the two middle ranges, and above the third cut point.

**Used in:** [Density categories](#density-categories) on this page.

```{r}

#| eval: false
```

## Density categories

Zero facilities is its own category; the other four are cut at the quartiles, each including its upper bound, as in the original code. It stops unless there are exactly three cut points in increasing order.

**Used in:** 6. Density categories ([Categories](define_exposure.qmd#categories)).

```{r}
#| label: fn-density-categories
#| eval: false
```

## Saving each provider's answers

Saves a provider's checked answers the first time and reads them back on a rerun, so a failure in one provider never means paying the others again.

**Used in:** 2. Cause of kidney failure ([Running, checking and saving each model](classify_esrd_causes.qmd#running-checking-and-saving-each-model)).

## Combining the models

One row per code with each model's category and reason; a category is accepted when at least `min_agreement` models give it (two of three in this project).

**Used in:** 2. Cause of kidney failure ([Agreement](classify_esrd_causes.qmd#agreement)).

```{r}

#| eval: false
```

## Reporting the local models

For each model that answers but does not vote: how many codes it answered once with a code from the list, how many it left unanswered, how many answers carried text that is not a code in the list, how many codes it answered more than once, and how often it gave the category the voting models accepted. Tested on synthetic answers with a known count of each.

**Used in:** 2. Cause of kidney failure ([What the local models showed](classify_esrd_causes.qmd#what-the-local-models-showed)).

```{r}
#| label: fn-local-model-report
#| eval: false
```
